label: input token e during the original phase
explanation: Token detector: fires on every original-phase step where the input token is e (precision 1.0 on dev), at any position and any L. Strongest on the first e of the sequence (top activations are e at t=0); a repeated e in the same sequence fires more weakly (about 0.4-0.6 of max in the examples). Silent on every other token, silent at the delimiter, and essentially silent in the copy phase. The roughly 1% of activations it misses are faint copy-phase firings at recall_idx 1-2 (where e is fed back as input), which carry almost no mass.

issues: On the test split the predicate (in_tok==e)&(phase==0) scores precision 1.000, recall 0.989, F1 0.995 and mass recall 0.9995, which matches the report. There are 0 false positives.

All 1176 missed activations are copy-phase steps where the input is e, at recall_idx 1-2 (mostly 3 on dev), with activations of 0.00-0.07 of max and about 0.05% of the mass. They come from short L=3-4 sequences where e is fed back as an input. This is faint and not a meaningful class. The label could say 'input e (essentially only in the original phase)'.

The in_first claims hold. Adding in_first==1 gives F1 0.946. The in_first==0 subset fires at precision 1.0 but its coverage is concentrated in the lowest activation quartiles (0.196 of the bottom quartile, 0.0 of the top quartile), so a repeated e is weaker.

Strongest at t=0 holds: all of (e & t==0)'s coverage falls in the top activation quartile. A small unstated nuance: per-firing mass declines with position (t=0 is about 1.21e-5 mass per firing versus about 0.81e-5 at t=4), so magnitude falls off with original position as well as with being a repeat.

In the copy phase the e input fires on only 1.3% of steps (precision 0.013), so 'almost silent in the copy phase' is accurate. No other token fires anywhere, and the feature never fires at the delimiter.
